prints.name: A little character. A lot of heart.
prints.description: Our first original ornament: two rounded characters, recessed eyes and a softly rounded heart on a shared base. The first physical prototype follows several rounds of design refinement.
prints.estimateNote: Completed, as reported by the owner. Settings are from the saved print package; size is from CAD, not a physical measurement. Material includes generated supports; extra startup purge may add to it. Actual weight, duration, base flatness and joint strength have not been measured or tested.
prints.credit: Original model: designed in OpenSCAD by Codex with Huzaifa’s direction and iterative feedback. · Printed on the Bambu Lab A1.
notes: Quality
Photos show clean rounded bodies and readable eyes and ears. Visible terraces on the feet, fine wisps and rough spots around the arm and heart tip still need attention.
Learned
Even 0.16 mm layers leave steps on shallow curves. Raising the heart tip preserved its silhouette, but added a delicate area needing supports and careful cleanup.
Next time
Remove remaining wisps and support nubs gently. Test finer or adaptive layers on a small sample, then review seam placement and support contacts before a refined reprint.

prints.name: One boat. Two beginnings.
prints.description: The last of the white sample became the beginning of another boat. A filament-runout pause let us continue with the new gray PLA.
prints.estimateNote: Slicer estimates exclude the extended changeover pause and extra loading/purge material. No photograph was recorded for this print.
prints.credit: Model: 3DBenchy by Creative Tools. · Printed from the printer’s bundled file.
notes: Quality
Completed successfully; the owner reports that it looks great. No photo inspection or strength test was performed.
Learned
The runout sensor paused at layer 55. After manually loading gray PLA, the same job resumed; compatible PLA colors can bond as successive layers.
Next time
Inspect any restart boundary on functional parts. Use an uninterrupted print when comparing surface finish, so the pause is not another variable.

prints.name: A little tool, made here.
prints.description: The first useful print: a lightweight scraper, with a sloping blade that turned into a lesson about layers.
prints.estimateNote: Material and time are from the saved print file, not measurements. Loading and startup purge use extra filament.
prints.credit: Model: Bed scraper by JernejP. · Included with the printer.
notes: Quality
Sits flat without rocking. The openings look clean, and the underside has a consistent texture from the build plate.
Learned
A sloping surface becomes tiny terraces when printed in layers. At 0.20 mm, those steps are easy to see across the blade.
Next time
Print the same design at 0.10 mm and compare the blade. Keep the material, orientation and physical shell thickness comparable.

prints.name: Every adventure needs a boat.
prints.description: The little white boat that started it all. Our first finished print, after setup, calibration and learning to load filament.
prints.estimateNote: Filament use is an approximate owner estimate. Layer height and print duration have not been verified for this job.
prints.credit: Model: 3DBenchy by Creative Tools. · Printed from the printer’s bundled file.
notes: Quality
The boat sits flush. Photos show a complete hull and cabin, with a few fine wisps of stringing around the openings.
Learned
Loading is complete when melted filament actually exits the nozzle—not just when the strand reaches the guide tube.
Next time
Keep this boat as a baseline. Inspect fine strands and the roof under consistent lighting before changing settings.
